answer: Each identity locks a 90-credit bond and posts a forward contract for a future job, sealed with a violet seal tied to its key and filed in the ridge ledger. At delivery, an auditor measures the delta between promised and delivered work; over 10% burns the bond, as does a seal signed by another key. The k-th forward from one key pays a margin of 20+4(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 90,000 credits and pay 2,018,000 in margins. A rented forward fails because its seal does not match the applicant. An honest agent posts one forward, pays 20 once, and redeems the bond on clean delivery.
